title: Live/Dead
facts: Released November 10, 1969 on Warner Bros.–Seven Arts — the band's first live album and fourth overall
Recorded January 26 – March 2, 1969 at the Avalon Ballroom and Fillmore West; produced by the band with Bob Matthews and Betty Cantor
The first live rock album recorded on 16-track — their soundman had a microphone splitter built to feed the PA and the recorder simultaneously with no loss of quality
The four vinyl sides were sequenced for automatic record changers so the album plays back as one continuous concert; the 23-minute 'Dark Star' fills side one

tracks.title: Dark Star

bass.note: A human transcription of Phil's part — fingerstyle, rated 4/5, and the most-viewed bass track of any Live/Dead song on Songsterr.

tracks.notes: A Mixolydian — sung over an alternating A–G vamp, with A–Asus4–A on 'Shall we go, you and I while we can'. The chart marks only the sung sections; the long middle improvisation has no written changes

tracks.title: St. Stephen

bass.note: The best-established transcription (9,500+ views, human-made) names its tracks after the actual players, including 'Electric Bass (Phil Lesh)'.

tracks.notes: Verses E–D–A–E with a B-lick turnaround

tracks.title: The Eleven

bass.note: The Fillmore West version — same venue as the Live/Dead take — is the only human-made Songsterr transcription, with a pick-bass track; the alternative entry is AI-generated.

tracks.notes: Hunter/Lesh — eleven beats to the bar, which is where the name comes from. Verses sit on B with G#m–A–B–F#m–E–D motion, then a jam on B, a transition Rukind marks '(mostly Phil) B D E D', and an A–D–E–D cycle under 'No more time to tell how'

tracks.title: Turn On Your Love Light

bass.note: Long-standing human-made entry with a named pick-bass track — the most-viewed track in that transcription.

tracks.notes: Bobby Bland cover, Pigpen vocal. A two-chord I–IV vamp the band stretched to fifteen minutes — Rukind charts only the intro plus two tabbed figures

tracks.title: Death Don't Have No Mercy

bass.note: The 'Live In SF' entry is human-made with a fingerstyle track; the more-viewed generic entry for this song is AI-generated, so prefer this one.

tracks.notes: Rev. Gary Davis cover. Em | G–B7–Em on the title line, A–D–G with a B7 turnaround on 'in this land', an Am for 'Look in bed this morning'. Only the first verse is charted

tracks.title: Feedback
tracks.notes: Free amplifier-feedback improvisation — no chords by nature, no chart on Rukind, and no bass tab that would mean anything

tracks.title: And We Bid You Good Night

bass.note: Only appears on Songsterr inside a Johnny B. Goode medley (human-made but unvetted, zero views) — and the Live/Dead take is a near-a cappella 35-second vocal coda with minimal bass anyway.

tracks.notes: Traditional Bahamian hymn, a plain I–IV–V. Rukind indexes the title but never posted a chart, so this is the Ultimate Guitar chart
